paper_title: A Multi-Task Benchmark for Abusive Language Detection in Low-Resource   Settings
caption: : Task-wise Class Distributions
model_annotation: The chart displays the class distributions of abusive language detection tasks, comparing two categories: Abusive and Not Abusive. The Abusive category is divided into eight slices, including Political, Other, Negative, Mixed, Racial, Sexist, Religious, and one slice labeled only as Negative. The colors of the slices vary, with Negative, Other, and Political being larger and more prominent, colored in different shades of blue, while the remaining slices are smaller and colored in white and shades of blue. The Not Abusive category is also divided into eight slices, including Other, Positive, Neutral, and Mixed, with varying shades of brown. There are percentage labels inside some of the slices, and a legend is not explicitly provided, but the labels inside the slices indicate their corresponding proportions. The segments appear ordered in no particular way within their respective categories.
